questions.question: Who were the parents of William H. Ferber (b. December 1869, Ohio, d. 11 March 1903, Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio)?
questions.rationale: Central gatekeeper question for the project objective. William has no parent links in the tree. The 1870 and 1880 US Federal Census records are the primary tools: the 1870 census would capture him as an infant in his parents' household; the 1880 census at age ~10-11. His 1903 death record and Ohio vital records may also name parents. Identifying the parents directly enables research into family geographic origins (the second part of the objective).

items.rationale: William was born December 1869; the June 1870 census would capture him as an infant (under 1 year) in his parents' household. This is the highest-probability record for identifying both parents by name and learning their nativity (German vs. Ohio-born), which directly advances the origins question.

William would be approximately 10-11 years old in 1880, almost certainly still residing in parents' household. Nativity columns for both parents would reveal whether they were born in Germany, providing direct evidence for the family origins question.

William's death certificate (11 March 1903) may name his parents. Ohio death certificates by 1903 typically recorded father's name and mother's maiden name; the informant was likely his widow Emma, who would have known this information. Direct parentage evidence if complete.

Ohio began statewide birth registration in 1867; coverage in Hamilton County by December 1869 was improving. A birth record would directly name both parents. Worth checking even if coverage is spotty.

Re-examine the original image of William's 1890 marriage record (source SLJ6-N3L already in project). Marriage records of this period in Ohio sometimes named the groom's father as a consent-giver or witness; the image may contain more than the index entry captures.

items.jurisdiction: Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio, United States
items.rationale: The surname 'Ferber' is German; Cincinnati had a large German immigrant community with well-maintained Lutheran, Catholic, and Reformed church registers. A baptismal record for William (December 1869) or siblings would directly name both parents. Parents' marriage record in a German church would confirm the family unit and potentially give German hometown of origin.

If William's father died before 1910, Hamilton County probate records (wills, administrations) would name heirs including William. A will naming William as a son is direct parentage evidence. Useful if census and vital-record approaches yield only a name hypothesis needing confirmation.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Research Question

Who were the parents of William H. Ferber (b. December 1869, Ohio, d. 11 March 1903, Cincinnati, Hamilton County, Ohio)?

## Summary of Research Attempted

This research session established a question (q_001) and a nine-item research plan (pl_001) targeting the records most likely to identify William H. Ferber's parents. The planned searches, in priority order, were: (1) 1870 US Federal Census, Hamilton County — William as infant in parents' household; (2) 1880 US Federal Census — William as child, ~age 10–11; (3) William's 1903 Ohio death certificate — may name parents; (4) Ohio birth record, December 1869 — may name parents directly; (5) re-examination of William's 1890 marriage record image for father's name; (6–7) Cincinnati city directories 1860s–1880s on FamilySearch and Ancestry; (8) German church records, Cincinnati, 1860–1875 — baptismal and marriage registers; (9) Hamilton County probate records 1880–1910.

Execution of every planned search was blocked by complete infrastructure failure. The genealogy MCP server (providing `record_search`, `research_append`, `research_log_append`, and all related tools) was confirmed TOOL_NOT_FOUND across four independent agent contexts. WebFetch, WebSearch, Bash, and PowerShell were all permission-denied in don't-ask mode. Two log entries (log_001, log_002) document the exhausted retry attempts.

## Evidentiary State

No records were retrieved. No assertions about William H. Ferber's parentage exist in this project. The existing tree (tree.gedcomx.json) records William's birth (December 1869, Ohio), death (11 March 1903, Cincinnati), and marriage (Emma Becker, 10 September 1890), but contains no parent links and no sibling data.

## Conclusion

The question of William H. Ferber's parentage is **not proved** at this time. This outcome reflects an infrastructure limitation, not a determination that the evidence does not exist. The 1870 and 1880 US Federal Census records are the highest-priority next searches; both are indexed on FamilySearch and should capture William as a child in his parents' household. When the genealogy MCP server reconnects and/or web permissions are restored, this project should be re-invoked — the research plan (pl_001) is complete and ready to execute.
